conditions_attacked.1_question: Holds. Both predict conversion from MCI to AD/dementia among ADNI MCI participants from cognitive tests plus FreeSurfer MRI measures. P-186's input is anchored to the conversion time: it classifies trajectories of two observed follow-up readings plus a forecast of the next reading, which it calls 'the forecasted marker value at the time of conversion' (p. 8). P-156 predicts from the baseline visit alone with an open horizon. These are horizon and input-representation differences, which the rule allows.
conditions_attacked.2_metric: Holds. ROC-AUC with ROC-AUC. P-186's value is the average over the 5 outer folds (Figure 5, 'average AUC'); P-156's is one held-out test set.
conditions_attacked.3_matched_figure: Holds. P-186 prints no baseline-only and no observed-two-visit-only result. Its only other condition is the ground-truth AUC using the actually observed third reading (NM+MRI 1 year 98%, Table 5), which moves further from P-156, not closer. P-186's unimodal results (1 year NM 91.5%, MRI 90.5%; 6 months MRI 88%) are not P-156's condition, which is multimodal and baseline-only; even the lowest, 0.88 (Hanley-McNeil 49/70: [0.813, 0.947]), excludes 0.81, if only just. P-156 prints no longitudinal model, and its per-modality results are cross-validation distributions in Fig. 3 with no numbers. Nothing reconciles the pair.
conditions_attacked.4_uncertainty: Holds; recomputed. P-186 0.957, Hanley-McNeil 35/50: SE 0.0249, [0.908, 1.000]. P-156 0.81 on the test set of 841 - 672 = 169 patients; class sizes not printed, about 58/111 at the cohort's 288/841 converter rate: SE 0.0377, [0.736, 0.884]. Each estimate lies outside the other's interval; two-sample z = 0.147/sqrt(0.0249^2 + 0.0377^2) = 3.25. P-186's 6-month 0.912 (49/70, [0.854, 0.970]) also excludes 0.81.
conditions_attacked.5_performance_validity: Holds by the letter: 0.957 < 0.97 and P-156's 0.81 is far below. P-186's figure carries three sources of optimism: features scaled before the train-test split (p. 4); markers ranked by t-tests 'on baseline biomarker readings' with no statement that the ranking is repeated inside the folds, while Figure 1 applies 'Marker Ranking' to the 'Full Normalized Longitudinal Dataset (n=85)'; and the reported marker-set size (9) is the best of all sizes tried (Table 5, Figure 5). These are candidate explanations, not a Section 3.5 exclusion.
conditions_attacked.6_record: The record's 0.957 is the 1-year NM+MRI result on n = 85; the registry's P-186 Best_Metric (0.912) is the 6-month result. Both are printed, and neither changes the verdict.

figures.P-186: NM+MRI, 1 year ahead: AUC 0.957 (5-fold CV average), n = 85 (35 MCIp / 50 MCIs); Hanley-McNeil SE 0.0249, 95% CI [0.908, 1.000]. 6 months ahead: 0.912, n = 119 (49/70), CI [0.854, 0.970]. Ground-truth (observed third reading) 0.98 and 0.942, not the compared figures.
figures.P-156: EI stacking with random forest: AUC 0.81 on a held-out 20% test set (169 of 841; about 58 progressed / 111 stable); Hanley-McNeil SE 0.0377, 95% CI [0.736, 0.884]. XGBoost 0.68 and autoencoder 0.79 on the same test set.

candidate_explanations: Input anchored to the conversion time (P-186) against a baseline-only input (P-156). P-186: 'The method proposed in this paper has recorded the highest classification AUC of 95.7% predominantly because of involving the forecasted marker value at the time of conversion as a classification feature.' (p. 8; the 'fi' ligature and curly apostrophes in the extracts are normalised to ASCII throughout this file). P-156: 'based only on data collected at baseline when they were diagnosed with MCI' (p. 3). P-186 prints no baseline-only comparator, so this is not shown to be sufficient.

Outcome window: conversion 'any time before the last follow-up time, i.e., 36th month' (P-186, p. 3) against 'The most recent diagnosis given to each patient (Final DX) was the outcome predicted' (P-156, p. 4).

Supervised marker selection apparently outside the folds and best-subset reporting (P-186): 'We perform two sampled Student's T-tests on baseline biomarker readings and then sift them according to their ranks' (p. 4); Table 5 reports the best marker-set size for each setting.
Pre-split scaling (P-186): 'We scale all features to have values between 0 and 1 before the train-test split.' (p. 4)

Cohort subset and completeness filter: an ADNI-1 subsample with complete consecutive readings, 'Subjects with missing values at designated follow-up times are ignored' (P-186, p. 3), n = 85, against 841 baseline E/LMCI patients from ADNI 1/2/GO (P-156).

Feature set and missing data (P-156): modalities with 30% or more missing values dropped, including PET and DTI, the rest KNN-imputed; CSF, demographics and APOE4 added. 'Several of the TADPOLE data modalities consisted of features that were missing for at least 30 % of the MCI patients' (p. 2).

Validation: a 5-fold CV average on 85 subjects (P-186) against one random 80/20 split (P-156): 'A randomly sampled 80 % subset of this cohort was used to train all the predictive models for the target problem.' (p. 3)
results.reason: I could not show a failed condition. P-186's only other condition (the observed third reading, 0.98) widens the gap, its unimodal results are not P-156's condition, and P-156 prints no longitudinal or numbered per-modality result. The recomputed intervals, [0.908, 1.000] against [0.736, 0.884], do not overlap (z = 3.25), and 0.957 is below the 0.97 exclusion. The pair qualifies. The report should add that P-186's marker ranking appears to have been done on all 85 subjects before cross-validation and that the reported marker-set size is the best of those tried, so its 0.957 is optimistic.

conditions_attacked.1_question: Holds. Both predict MCI-to-AD conversion among ADNI MCI participants with a model that includes structural MRI (P-229: 90 AAL grey-matter volumes only; P-178: hippocampal and ventricular volumes among nine features). P-178 is early MCI with an open horizon (mean 5.02 years to conversion); P-229 is all MCI with a 36-month window. Cohort subset and horizon are allowed differences. The record's P-229 figure (71.05%) is the SCD-to-MCI result on CLAS; I re-read P-229's MCI result from the PDF, Table IV on page 30: 'IADT (Ours) 73.54 73.00 75.70 69.46 76.55' (ACC, BAC, AUC, SEN, SPE).
conditions_attacked.2_metric: Holds for AUC with AUC. Accuracy is not usable: P-178's SVC reaches 0.900 accuracy with AUC 0.52-0.55 by predicting the majority class (Table 4).
conditions_attacked.3_matched_figure: Holds. P-178's other models are 6 features (no MRI volumes, no APOE4; AUC 0.88) and 13 features (adds RAVLT; AUC 0.93); it prints no MRI-only model, no 36-month result and no all-MCI analysis. P-229 has no cognitive predictors and no early-MCI or open-horizon analysis. P-229's Table IV comparators (baseline 69.20, TCA 62.24, GFK 70.08, SA 70.09, CORAL 69.84, VoxCNN 74.74) are other methods under P-229's own condition and lie still further from P-178. Nothing reconciles the pair.
conditions_attacked.4_uncertainty: Holds; recomputed. P-229 0.757, Hanley-McNeil 167/226: SE 0.0252, [0.708, 0.806]. P-178's test unit is visits: from Table 4 (non-converter precision 0.952, recall 0.978, accuracy 0.936) and the text's '20 EMCI_C ground truth subjects and 9 EMCI_NC ground truth subjects were incorrectly classified' (p. 12), the test set is about 409 non-converter and 44 converter visits (453, against the text's 1806 - 1354 = 452), from 95 patients (about 11-12 converters). Subject-level Hanley-McNeil 12/83: SE 0.040, [0.882, 1.000]; 11/84: [0.878, 1.000]; visit-level 44/408: [0.919, 1.000]. Each estimate lies outside the other's interval at every choice; z = 0.203/sqrt(0.040^2 + 0.0252^2) = 4.29.
conditions_attacked.5_performance_validity: Holds by the letter: 0.96 < 0.97, and P-229's 0.757 is far below. P-178's figure is optimistic: the feature set and the sampling method were chosen on the same 75/25 test split with no separate validation set (13 to 9 features 'our accuracy rose to 93.6%'; Table 6), there is no external cohort, and at its operating threshold the model detects only about 24 of 44 converter visits (0.55). Not a Section 3.5 exclusion.
conditions_attacked.6_record: The record misreads P-229 (71.05% is the SCD task); the pair is judged on Table IV, which P-229 prints. P-178's Table 1 (402/402 oversampled test records) conflicts with the Table 4 arithmetic, which fits the 452 un-oversampled test visits.

figures.P-229: IADT, pMCI vs sMCI (393 ADNI MCI, 167/226, 36 months; classifier trained on labelled AD/NC with the MCI as unlabelled target): AUC 0.757, ACC 73.54%; Hanley-McNeil SE 0.0252, 95% CI [0.708, 0.806].
figures.P-178: 9-feature random forest: AUC 0.96, accuracy 0.936 on the visits of 95 held-out patients (derived about 44 converter / 409 non-converter visits); subject-level Hanley-McNeil 12/83 SE 0.040, CI [0.882, 1.000]; visit-level 44/408 CI [0.919, 1.000]. 6-feature model without MRI or APOE4: AUC 0.88.
figures.comparison: Intervals exclude each other in both directions; z = 4.29.

candidate_explanations: Predictor set: P-178 adds cognitive and functional scores (ADAS13, ADAS11, FAQ, MMSE), APOE4, age and race to two MRI volumes; P-229 uses grey-matter ROI volumes alone. P-178's model without MRI and APOE4 still reaches AUC 0.88, but it is not an MRI-only comparison. P-178: 'We also tested a 6-feature group, which removed the RAVLT variables as well as the biomarker data; however, this saw the worst accuracy of the three groups at 89.2%.' (p. 7)

Horizon and label: conversion by the last visit (mean 5.02 years; 'the Clinical Dementia Rating was used to make this determination based on the value of their last visit's diagnosis', P-178 p. 3) against 'The pMCI subjects have converted to AD within 36 months while sMCI have not.' (P-229, p. 10).

Label-free transfer training in P-229: 'A total of 393 MCI subjects (167 pMCI, 226 sMCI) with structural MRIs are used as the unlabeled target domain, while AD and NC samples are adopted as the labeled source domain.' (p. 10). P-178 trains on converter labels directly.

Population: early MCI only in P-178 ('383 Early Mild Cognitive Impairment (EMCI) patients were gathered from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI)', p. 1) against unselected ADNI MCI in P-229.

Unit of analysis: P-178 trains and tests on visit records, several per patient ('we train a 1000 tree random forest model on 2412 exam visits', p. 7), so its AUC is visit-level; its Table 1 test counts (402/402) contradict its Table 4 figures.

Model selection on the test split (P-178): 'While initially, using all 13-features seemed to provide the highest accuracy at 91.6%, we found that by removing the RAVLT features, our accuracy rose to 93.6% in the 9-feature group.' (p. 7)
results.reason: I could not show a failed condition. P-229's MCI-conversion AUC, which I re-read from its Table IV (0.757, [0.708, 0.806]), and P-178's 0.96 exclude each other whether P-178's interval is taken at the subject level ([0.882, 1.000]) or the visit level ([0.919, 1.000]), and neither paper prints a figure under the other's condition. 0.96 is below 0.97. The pair qualifies, on the figures the papers print rather than the record's misread 71.05%. The report should add that P-178's AUC is visit-level, that its feature set was chosen on the same test split, and that its tables disagree on what the test set contained.

conditions_attacked.1_question: Holds. Both ask whether naturalistic driving data with demographics separate older community drivers with MCI or dementia from cognitively healthy older drivers. P-69's positive label is a diagnosis made during up to 44 months of monitoring among drivers intact at enrolment; P-331's is status at baseline (with a one-year-ahead analysis). The rule allows timing differences; they are recorded as candidate explanations.
conditions_attacked.2_metric: Holds formally (accuracy with accuracy), but raw accuracy cannot carry the pair. In P-69's test set the rule 'everyone is healthy' scores 90/105 = 0.857, which is itself outside P-331's Wilson interval [0.598, 0.763], and P-69's random forest on driving features alone scores 0.905 while detecting 5 of 15 impaired drivers. P-69 says so itself: 'Accuracy may no longer be a good metric to evaluate the performance of a classifier over an imbalanced dataset, because it is biased toward the majority class.' (p. 9). The qualification therefore rests on the prevalence-free balanced accuracy derived from the printed counts, as the reader did. P-69's confusion-matrix orientation is confirmed on p. 11 ('the diagonal elements are the correctly classified healthy (i.e., 90) and dementia (i.e., 11) case numbers').
conditions_attacked.3_matched_figure: Holds for P-69's primary model, but fragile. P-69 prints six results on P-331's input channel (demographics + driving; Table 3, Models 4 and 5, three classifiers each). Balanced accuracy from its confusion matrices: Model 4 logistic 0.778 [0.654, 0.901], random forest 0.700 [0.576, 0.824], ResBlocks 0.767 [0.640, 0.893]; Model 5 (with I-score selection) logistic 0.900 [0.828, 0.972], random forest 0.850 [0.737, 0.963], ResBlocks 0.867 [0.754, 0.979]. Against P-331's Model 4 (0.643, [0.556, 0.730]): the random forest without I-score agrees in both directions (z = 0.74); ResBlocks and logistic without I-score lie outside P-331's interval, though P-331's estimate lies inside or just outside theirs (z = 1.58, 1.75); all three I-score models differ (z = 3.08, 2.84, 4.45). Architecture and feature selection are allowed differences, and P-69's primary result under this input does not agree, so condition 3 is not failed. But the gap rests on P-69's I-score-selected models. Driving only: P-69 Model 2 0.667-0.700 against P-331 Model 2 0.545 [0.453, 0.636]; P-69's estimates are outside P-331's interval, and P-331's lies at or just outside P-69's lower bounds (0.547-0.576). Demographics only: P-69 ResBlocks Model 1 reaches 0.839 [0.725, 0.953], close to its headline 0.867, while P-69's logistic and random-forest Model 1 (0.644, 0.656) agree with P-331's Model 1 (0.613, [0.523, 0.703]).
conditions_attacked.4_uncertainty: Holds for the headline pair. Accuracy 0.962 (101/105, Wilson [0.906, 0.985]) against 0.686 (81/118, [0.598, 0.763]); on the matched inputs, P-331 Model 4 0.670 ([0.581, 0.748]). Balanced accuracy 0.867 (SE 0.057) against 0.668 (SE 0.044): each lies outside the other's interval, z = 2.74. The Wald SE for 15 impaired cases is rough; using Wilson bounds for P-69's two class rates (11/15 [0.481, 0.891], 90/90 [0.959, 1.000]) gives a balanced-accuracy range of about [0.72, 0.95], which still excludes 0.668.
conditions_attacked.5_performance_validity: Holds by the letter: P-69's 0.962 accuracy is below 0.97 and its AUC is 0.87. The figure is internal, from one random split with 15 impaired test cases. Section 3.3 describes the I-score module selection as 'Applying BDA to the dementia dataset' before the train/test split is introduced (Section 4.3.1), while Algorithm 2 names its input a 'Training Set'; the text does not settle whether the 15 test cases were kept out of the selection. P-331 uses nested LOSO-CV on 118 subjects.
conditions_attacked.6_record: The figures the record compares (96% and 68.64%) are printed; the record omits the prevalence difference and the incident-versus-prevalent labels.

figures.P-331: Subject-level nested LOSO-CV (72 impaired / 46 healthy). Model 6: accuracy 81/118 = 0.686, Wilson [0.598, 0.763]; balanced accuracy 0.668 (recall 54/72, specificity 27/46), SE 0.044, CI [0.582, 0.755]. Model 4 (demographics + driving): accuracy 79/118 = 0.670, [0.581, 0.748]; balanced accuracy 0.643 (55/72, 24/46), CI [0.556, 0.730]. Model 2 (driving only): balanced accuracy 0.545 (44/72, 22/46), CI [0.453, 0.636]. Model 1 (demographics only): 0.613, CI [0.523, 0.703]. One year ahead: 74/105 = 0.705, [0.612, 0.784].
figures.P-69: Single random test set of 90 healthy / 15 impaired. Model 5 ResBlocks: accuracy 101/105 = 0.962, Wilson [0.906, 0.985]; AUC 0.87; balanced accuracy 0.867 (11/15, 90/90), SE 0.057, CI [0.754, 0.979]. Matched-input Model 4 without I-score: random forest balanced accuracy 0.700 [0.576, 0.824] (accuracy 0.914), ResBlocks 0.767 [0.640, 0.893], logistic 0.778 [0.654, 0.901]. Demographics-only ResBlocks: 0.839 [0.725, 0.953]. All-healthy rule: accuracy 0.857.
figures.comparison: Headline accuracy z = 5.9 and balanced accuracy z = 2.74. On the matched inputs without I-score, P-69's random forest agrees with P-331 (z = 0.74) and its other two classifiers are within two-sample uncertainty (z = 1.58, 1.75), though outside P-331's interval.

candidate_explanations: Class mix and operating point: 14% impaired in P-69's test set against 61% in P-331. P-69's models classify all 90 healthy drivers correctly in most configurations, while P-331 tunes toward recall: 'The final model selection is based on the F1-score, optimizing the balance between precision and recall.' (P-331, p. 13). P-69: 'We randomly select 90 healthy and 15 dementia data points as the test data, and use the remaining 2826 healthy and 46 dementia data points as the training data.' (p. 8). Balanced accuracy at one threshold is not threshold-free, and P-331 reports no AUC.

I-score module selection in P-69 carries the gap: without it, P-69's matched-input results (0.700-0.778) are within two-sample uncertainty of P-331's 0.643; with it, they rise to 0.850-0.900. P-69: 'Applying BDA to the dementia dataset, we present the top five most predictive variable modules from I-score in Table 1.' (Section 3.3). Whether the test cases were excluded from this selection is not stated.

Demographic and site signal in P-69: its top I-score module includes 'Age (at the time of study entry), Region (study site)' (p. 6), and its ResBlocks on demographics alone reaches balanced accuracy 0.839, close to the headline 0.867. The report should not present the pair as a disagreement about what driving data alone can do.

Timing and population behind the positive label: 'if one participant was healthy at the beginning of the study but gradually moved to MCI, unspecified dementia, and then Alzheimer's disease, we will assign a value of one for this participant.' (P-69, p. 4) against baseline status assessed by clinicians (P-331).

Label source: yearly interview labels in P-69 ('participants were interviewed annually. Thus, we have each participant's yearly diagnosis label.', p. 4) against assessment by two dementia-specialist clinicians in P-331.
Case mix: 'Among these 61 patients, 36 have MCI, 8 Alzheimer's disease, and 17 have other or unspecified dementia.' (P-69, p. 4) against 64 MCI and 8 dementia in P-331.

Monitoring length and feature representation: 10 to 44 months of monthly driving variables summarised by 48 time-series features each (P-69: 'for each time-dependent driving variable, 48 time-series features are extracted using tsfeatures() package', p. 4) against three months of weekly aggregated driving metrics (P-331).

Validation: one random split with 15 impaired test cases and SMOTE-balanced training (P-69: 'In this paper, we use SMOTE to balance the training data.', p. 8) against nested leave-one-subject-out CV with subject-level majority voting (P-331).
results.reason: I could not show a failed condition, but this pair is the most fragile of the four. Raw accuracy cannot carry it, because in P-69's test set the rule 'everyone is healthy' scores 0.857, itself outside P-331's interval. On balanced accuracy derived from the printed counts, the headline models still differ (0.867 against 0.668, z = 2.74), and P-69's primary model on P-331's inputs does not agree, so condition 3 holds. However, P-69's random forest without I-score selection on the same demographics-plus-driving inputs (0.700) agrees with P-331's Model 4 (0.643), and its other two classifiers without I-score are within two-sample uncertainty. The pair qualifies only as a gap carried by P-69's I-score-selected models, and the report should say so.

conditions_attacked.1_question: Holds. Both predict MCI-to-AD progression among ADNI MCI participants (ADNI1/GO/2/3 in both). The shared channel is structural MRI: three hippocampal T1 slices in P-356, FreeSurfer regional morphometry in P-244, which also includes clinical scores and APOE4. Under the rule a multimodal model matches when the compared channel is shared.
conditions_attacked.2_metric: Holds. ROC-AUC with ROC-AUC. P-356's is a binary AUC on a cleaned stable/progressive dichotomy; P-244's is a time-dependent AUC from a survival model. The estimand difference is recorded as a candidate explanation.
conditions_attacked.3_matched_figure: Holds. A horizon-matched figure exists, P-244's 3-year AUC of 0.914 (text p. 1 and the Fig. 7C legend), and it does not reconcile the pair. No input-matched figure exists. P-244's reduced models are single-variable survival models on MMSE (0.537-0.600) and APOE4 (0.564-0.681), neither of them MRI. P-356 prints no clinical model, and its 3D ResNet-18 (0.75) is also image-only. P-244's external AIBL check prints only C-indices in the text (0.752, [0.698, 0.807]). Its external 3- and 5-year AUCs are described only as showing 'consistently comparative performance with MMSE', with the numbers in Supplementary Fig. S15(D), which is not held. That is not a figure I can compare.
conditions_attacked.4_uncertainty: Holds; recomputed. P-356's 10 runs vary initialisation on a single test set ('Distribution of model performance metrics across 10 runs of the test set'), so a single-test-set interval applies. Hanley-McNeil 41/45 (15% of 575 at the constant ratio): SE 0.054, [0.634, 0.846]; the best run, 0.78, gives [0.681, 0.879]. P-244's 3-year 0.914: [0.892, 0.936] at 348/435, [0.865, 0.963] at one fold's 70/87, [0.858, 0.970] at 50/87, and [0.843, 0.985] even at 30/127. 0.74 (and 0.78) lie outside every P-244 interval, and 0.914 lies outside P-356's. z at fold size = 0.174/sqrt(0.0248^2 + 0.054^2) = 2.93.
conditions_attacked.5_performance_validity: Holds by the letter: the compared AUCs are 0.914 and 0.957, below 0.97, on n = 783 with an external AIBL check; P-356's is 0.74. Three points in P-244 raise doubt without meeting the exclusion. The text does not state that the Fig. 7C ROC curves are cross-validated, whereas the Fig. 7B C-indices are explicitly '5-fold cross-validated'. The AUC rises with horizon to 0.979 at 10 years. MMSE's time-dependent AUCs (0.537-0.600) sit below MMSE's own cross-validated C-index in Fig. 7B (0.681).
conditions_attacked.6_record: The record compares P-244's 5-year 0.957; the horizon-matched 3-year 0.914 was judged instead and gives the same result. The registry defects the reader listed do not affect the figures.

figures.P-356: ViT on three hippocampal T1 slices, sMCI (stable >= 3 years) vs pMCI (AD within 36 months), 575 subjects: test AUC 0.74 +/- 0.02 over 10 runs on one test set (range 0.72-0.78); test set about 86 (41/45); Hanley-McNeil SE 0.054, 95% CI [0.634, 0.846]. 3D ResNet-18: 0.75.
figures.P-244: Deep-AD, 783 ADNI MCI (348 converters, 435 censored), five-fold CV: time-dependent AUC MCI->AD 3 years 0.914, 5 years 0.957 (1 year 0.810, 10 years 0.979). No AUC interval or horizon class sizes printed; Hanley-McNeil for 0.914 from [0.892, 0.936] (348/435) to [0.843, 0.985] (30/127). Pattern C-index 0.718 [0.712, 0.725]; AIBL external C-index 0.752 [0.698, 0.807].
figures.comparison: Horizon-matched 0.914 against 0.74: each lies outside the other's interval at any plausible n; z = 2.93 at fold size.

candidate_explanations: Predictor set: P-244 adds baseline cognitive and clinical scores and APOE4 to FreeSurfer regional morphometry: 'we concatenated the baseline clinical features and neuroimaging features extracted from the MRI scans, embedded with t through a transformer encoder, to map to z.' (p. 3). P-356: 'In this work, we solely focused on MRI features' (p. 9). P-244 prints no MRI-only model, so this is not shown to be sufficient.

Estimand and censoring: a time-dependent AUC from a survival model over all MCI participants, 'of which 348 (44.44%) samples were converted from MCI to AD dementia while the others (55.56%) were right censored.' (P-244, p. 3), against a binary AUC on a cleaned dichotomy.

Label cleaning (P-356): 'Individuals in the sMCI group were categorized as stable if they retained this status for a minimum of three years and maintained it throughout all available follow-up assessments provided by ADNI.' Reverters were excluded (p. 3).

P-244's time-dependent AUCs are not stated to be cross-validated: 'As illustrated in the ROC curves evaluated at 1, 3, 5 and 10 years (Fig. 7(C)), our model achieved consistently impressive performance on predicting the progression time of AD dementia/MCI onset' (p. 12), whereas the C-index panel reads 'The violin plots showed the 5-fold cross-validated C-Index results for each variable.' (Fig. 7 caption).

The encoder is defined on the baseline features and the progression time t (posterior q(z|x,t)). The paper states that inference does not use t: 'In the inference stage, we only used data x at the starting point' (p. 4). The held text does not show how t is supplied at inference. This is weaker than the reader's version: the text claims baseline-only inference.

External check: in AIBL the Deep-AD C-index (0.752) is close to MMSE's (0.730), and 'A similar pattern of results in terms of AUC and DCA was observed on 3- and 5-year predictions, with consistently comparative performance with MMSE' (p. 14). The external AUCs are not printed in the main text.

The horizon-matched 3-year AUC (0.914) still lies outside P-356's interval [0.634, 0.846], and 0.74 lies outside P-244's interval at every plausible class size (lowest bound 0.843). Neither paper prints a result under the other's input condition, and neither compared figure reaches 0.97. The pair qualifies. The report should add that P-244's time-dependent AUCs are not stated to be cross-validated and rise with horizon, and that its external AUCs were only described as comparable with MMSE. It should also soften the progression-time concern, because P-244 states that inference uses baseline data only.
